nodes.title: One step of the tardiness computation

nodes.summary: The decision problem TOTAL TARDINESS accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding (natural numbers in binary), to an instance of TOTAL TARDINESS that is feasible, that is, whose jobs admit an ordering of total tardiness at most its bound. It rejects every bitstring that does not decode to an instance.
nodes.title: The TOTAL TARDINESS decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(J, K)$ of TOTAL TARDINESS with $n$ jobs is feasible when some ordering of its jobs, that is, some permutation $(j_1, \dots, j_n)$ of $(0, 1, \dots, n - 1)$, has total tardiness at most $K$.
nodes.title: Feasible TOTAL TARDINESS instances

nodes.summary: An instance of TOTAL TARDINESS is a pair $(J, K)$ consisting of a finite list $J = ((p_0, d_0), \dots, (p_{n-1}, d_{n-1}))$ of jobs, where job $j$ has processing time $p_j \in \mathbb{N}$ and due date $d_j \in \mathbb{N}$, and a bound $K \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Instances of TOTAL TARDINESS

nodes.summary: The TOTAL TARDINESS decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: TOTAL TARDINESS is NP-complete

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
